items.t: Air suspension strut leaks and the car sags
items.note: Owners report about $1,700 per strut and up to $8,500 for a dealer pair. Converting to conventional struts costs about $1,500.

items.t: Brake pedal sinks and braking feels weak
items.note: Covered by Hyundai's 15-year/unlimited-mile HECU warranty extension on 2011-2012 Equus. Without coverage, owners were quoted about $2,800 to $3,000.

items.t: ABS module can leak inside and catch fire (recall)

items.job: Replace wiper motor cover and seal
items.note: Hyundai also extended the wiper motor warranty to 10 years/100,000 miles on 2011-2013 Equus.

items.t: Brake lights may not come on (recall)

items.job: Replace shift solenoids or transmission electronic module
items.note: Hyundai's bulletins call for this before replacing the transmission. A full replacement costs far more.

Based on KBB, since no parts-plus-labor source was found: a 2014 Equus dealer replacement is $5,227-$5,619 total ($3,925-$4,209 parts). Labor hours are backed out of KBB's $1,302-$1,410 labor charge. Ask whether Hyundai's powertrain warranty still covers your car first.

items.t: Airbag light from a failed clock spring
items.note: Covered by Hyundai's 15-year/unlimited-mile clock spring warranty extension; confirm with your VIN.

items.t: Car pulls or alignment won't stay in spec
items.note: Ask the shop to follow Hyundai tracking bulletin TSB-11-SS-004 if a normal alignment does not fix the pull.

items.t: Leather dashboard cover shrinking or lifting
items.note: A dealer quoted about $4,500 because the windshield and dash must come out.
An owner paid $1,350 at an independent shop for a taillight; a dealer quoted $1,800.
Parts depend on what is found.
